summary: A snow weather: falling flakes, a white battlefield with wind-scoured drifts and churned mud, patchy snow on roofs, trees and the flat tops of vehicles, and thaws round fires and idling engines.
rationale: Snow is above all a change of appearance. A wide view over a town in falling snow shows the whole look at once (flakes, drifted ground, roofs that differ, trees holding it in lumps, mountains in the haze); a close-up shows how a tank that has been fighting carries it (patches on the flat tops, a bare engine deck); and one matched sheet shows the same town and the same moment of a tank battle under the overcast sky and in snow. A third still shows heat melting it, a fourth the drifts against a hedge and a wall: a burning wreck, a burning hedgerow and an idling tank in one frame. The flakes' drift, the shedding as a vehicle drives, a fired barrel going bare and the slow re-whitening once a fire is out are described in text.
